articles.originalTitle: Seven Sculpture Shows to See in New York, From Modernist Masterpieces to Contemporary Anti-Monuments - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Seven Sculpture Shows to See in New York
articles.excerpt: A series of seven sculpture exhibitions across New York, ranging from 15th-century bronzes to contemporary installations, coincides with Art Week NYC.
articles.content: New York is hosting a diverse array of sculpture exhibitions this fall, running alongside Art Week NYC events from November 11 to 14. Paula Cooper Gallery presents "Six Themes," revisiting works by Pop artist Claes Oldenburg, while Pietro Alexander features new sculptures by Charlie Engelman utilizing materials tied to California's natural and industrial past. At Andrew Edlin Gallery, works by Beverly Buchanan highlight her abstract paintings and handcrafted shack sculptures. Yossi Milo exhibits intricately carved clay vessels by Ibrahim Said, following his tenure as an inaugural artist in the Metropolitan Museum of Art and Vacheron Constantin Artisan Residency. The Frick Collection presents approximately 40 surviving Sienese bronze sculptures dating from 1450 to 1500. Karma features wooden abstractions produced between 1954 and 1968 by sculptor Thaddeus Mosley, who passed away in March at age 99. Additionally, David Nolan Gallery showcases Chakaia Booker's baroque-styled sculptures crafted from used automobile tires, alongside collages, photographs, and a tapestry.

articles.originalTitle: Hong Kong’s M+ Museum launches alliance with Centre Pompidou and MoMA as part of fifth anniversary celebrations—podcast - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Hong Kong's M+ Museum Marks Fifth Anniversary with Alliance
articles.excerpt: Hong Kong's M+ Museum is celebrating its fifth anniversary by launching a new cultural alliance with MoMA and the Centre Pompidou.
articles.content: Marking five years since its opening, Hong Kong's M+ Museum has welcomed over 2.5 million visitors annually for the past three consecutive years. To celebrate its anniversary, the institution has formed a new cultural alliance with the Museum of Modern Art in New York and the Centre Pompidou in Paris. According to M+ museum director Suhanya Raffel, the partnership unites three collecting institutions committed to supporting artistic innovation and public engagement through research and exchange. Board chairman Paulo Pong outlined upcoming programmes, including the M+ Restored Festival running from November 1 to December 27, the exhibition Hong Kong: Here and Beyond opening in March 2027, and the Public Conversation: 2026 Culture for the Planet Summit on November 6. Furthermore, the museum is launching the M+ Academy in November to provide resources, mentorship, and connections for current and emerging museum professionals.

articles.originalTitle: herzog & de meuron to convert former birkenstock warehouse into the eames institute museum - Designboom
articles.title: Herzog & de Meuron to Convert Former Birkenstock Campus into Museum
articles.excerpt: Herzog & de Meuron is transforming a former Birkenstock campus in Novato, California, into the Eames Institute Museum, with construction intended to begin in 2028.
articles.content: A former Birkenstock campus in Novato, California, is being reworked into the future museum of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity. Designed by Herzog & de Meuron, the project involves San Francisco practice EHDD as executive architect and Field Operations as landscape designer. Spanning approximately 88 acres, the cultural destination will feature exhibition spaces, workshops, a theater, and gardens. The existing campus, originally designed for publisher McGraw-Hill by Jan Lubicz-Nycz, features a recognizable roof assembled from repeated hyperbolic paraboloid shells. Herzog & de Meuron will organize the interior around a central hall while keeping the roof geometry visible. Following the masterplan submission to the City of Novato, major construction is intended to begin in 2028, with 2030 targeted for the museum opening.

articles.originalTitle: MoMA, Centre Pompidou, and M+ Will Treat Their Holdings as One Collection in Unprecedented Alliance - ARTnews.com
articles.title: MoMA, Centre Pompidou, and M+ Form Alliance to Treat Holdings as One Collection
articles.excerpt: MoMA, the Centre Pompidou, and M+ announced a cultural alliance to treat their respective holdings as a shared collection curated across three continents.
articles.content: Hong Kong's M+, the Museum of Modern Art in New York, and the Centre Pompidou in Paris have announced a cultural alliance to treat their holdings as a shared collection, curated by staff across three continents. The combined holdings of MoMA and the Pompidou total hundreds of thousands of objects, while M+ holds approximately 8,000 objects. Beginning in late 2027, works from M+ will be installed on long-term loan in MoMA galleries, followed by the opening of a long-term Centre Pompidou gallery at MoMA in 2028. Over the next five years, the partner institutions will co-organize an exhibition exploring the concept of the contemporary. A joint steering committee will meet monthly and hold annual in-person meetings. The Centre Pompidou is currently closed for a building restoration and is scheduled to reopen in 2030. Museum directors noted that the alliance goes beyond past exhibition loans by committing to long-term collaborative programs and sustainable shipping practices.

articles.originalTitle: Circularity Cabin by Takaaki Fuji + Yuko Fuji Architecture - Architectural Record
articles.title: Circularity Cabin Designed for Disassembly and Relocation in Zushi
articles.excerpt: Takaaki Fuji and Yuko Fuji Architecture designed Circularity Cabin in Zushi, Japan, as a compact two-story home built entirely from off-the-shelf lumber to be unbolted and relocated.
articles.content: Completed in March 2023 in Zushi, Japan, Circularity Cabin by Takaaki Fuji + Yuko Fuji Architecture serves as a primary residence for a couple and their child. Because roughly half the site lies within a planned road widening, the compact two-story home was designed with the certainty of future demolition. The structure is assembled entirely from off-the-shelf lumber using only bolts and screws without adhesives or cut joinery, allowing it to be unbolted, stored, and reconstructed elsewhere or returned to the timber market. The design exposes all screws, bolts, and pipes, enabling residents to perform maintenance using local hardware store materials. The street-facing side features a solid wooden wall, while light and air enter through clerestory windows oriented via computational fluid dynamics. The construction uses mineral-based structural boards and vertical sawara cypress boarding for the exterior, avoiding plywood and adhesives. The total construction cost for the project was 104,000 dollars.

articles.originalTitle: New York’s Socrates Sculpture Park rebuilds for resilience and expands - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Socrates Sculpture Park Expands and Rebuilds for Climate Resilience
articles.excerpt: New York's Socrates Sculpture Park is expanding with a 1-acre addition featuring works by Mark di Suvero, while parts of its campus undergo seawall reconstruction.
articles.content: The New York City Department of Parks & Recreation has begun seawall reconstruction at Socrates Sculpture Park on the Queens waterfront, an area that was submerged during Superstorm Sandy in 2012. Funded by the Federal Emergency Management Agency, the work requires much of the five-acre campus to remain closed until next spring. Marking its 40th anniversary, the park is transforming a dormant storage area on its southern edge into a one-acre expansion called The Point, which will open on 31 October with a long-term installation of three monumental sculptures by founding artist Mark di Suvero. Executive director Shaun Leonardo stated that the project connects the park's future to its founding story. The sculptures, created between 1995 and 2017, involve dynamic elements such as swings and a spinning titanium piece. Furthermore, a workforce development program for residents of nearby public housing has been relaunched with support from the Ford Foundation and Urban Upbound. The park's leadership emphasizes that its landscaping strategies focus on climate resilience, soil rehabilitation, and flood mitigation.

articles.originalTitle: Art Dealer Family the Nahmads Are the Consignors Behind $80 M. Kandinsky Set to Break a Record at Christie’s - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Nahmad Family Revealed as Consignors of Record-Bound Kandinsky Painting at Christie's
articles.excerpt: The prominent art dealer Nahmad family has been identified as the consignors behind Wassily Kandinsky's Betonte Ecken, which is expected to fetch up to $80 million at Christie's.
articles.content: Ahead of the major fall auctions, the consignor of Wassily Kandinsky's 1922–1923 painting Betonte Ecken has been identified as the prominent art dealer and collector family, the Nahmads. Carrying an estimate of $60 million to $80 million at Christie's New York, the colorful abstraction is the highest-priced lot in the upcoming sales. The auction house indicated that the work carries a third-party guarantee ensuring it will surpass the artist's previous auction record of $44.8 million set in 2023. Painted in Weimar while Kandinsky taught at the Bauhaus, the artwork has a documented provenance that includes the Jacob Hecht Auction House in Berlin, early US abstract art supporter Hilla Rebay, the Solomon R. Guggenheim Museum, and various private collections before reaching the present owners. Exhibition catalogs from the past 25 years have previously listed the Nahmad Collection as the owner of the painting. Christie's declined to comment on the matter, and the Nahmad family did not respond by press time.

articles.originalTitle: Beyond Affordable Housing: Integrating Civic Infrastructure in US Mixed-Use Developments - ArchDaily
articles.title: Integrating Civic Infrastructure and Affordable Housing in the United States
articles.excerpt: Throughout the twentieth century, affordable housing in the United States was conceived as a residential category separate from broader urban functions. Today, its provision remains closely tied to economic mechanisms and regulatory standards.
articles.content: For much of the twentieth century, affordable housing in the United States was conceived as a distinct residential category, shaped by financing practices that separated housing for lower-income residents from broader civic and commercial functions. Federal housing legislation and urban renewal policies contributed to the construction of large residential developments financed and managed independently of surrounding urban infrastructure. Documented consequences of this approach include concentrated poverty, deteriorating buildings, unequal access to services, and the eventual demolition of prominent public housing projects. Today, the provision of affordable housing is closely tied to economic and regulatory mechanisms determining feasibility, ranging from land values and construction costs to zoning regulations and public subsidies. Housing credit programs play a significant role in financing affordable rental housing, while competitive resource allocation and pressure to maximize housing delivery place considerable emphasis on regulatory compliance across the sector.

articles.originalTitle: inside the parisian hotel renovation where british club culture meets haussmannian architecture - Designboom
articles.title: Historic Hotel Westminster in Paris Undergoes Extensive Restoration
articles.excerpt: Located on rue de la Paix in Paris, the historic Hotel Westminster has received its fifth star following an extensive restoration led by interior architect Laurent Maugoust and designer Helen Stephens.
articles.content: Situated on rue de la Paix between Place Vendôme and Palais Garnier in Paris, the historic Hotel Westminster underwent an extensive restoration led by interior architect Laurent Maugoust and designer Helen Stephens. Completed one year ago, the project preserves architectural elements accumulated throughout the building's history while introducing contemporary interiors. Awarded its fifth star in 2025, the property traces its origins back to 1802 when Napoleon Bonaparte commissioned the development of the district. The Haussmannian silhouette, established by architect Jacques Marcel Aubertin between 1905 and 1907, remains intact alongside marble fireplaces and herringbone oak parquet floors across its 102 rooms. Duke's Bar preserves its British heritage through dark wood paneling and an original fireplace, reflecting its history as a gathering place for historical figures including Winston Churchill and Coco Chanel. Meanwhile, Helen Stephens redesigned Le Céladon restaurant, incorporating shades of green that reference the nearby Tuileries Garden and the Vendôme Column.

articles.originalTitle: kengo kuma’s brick towers frame open-air pools at copenhagen’s upcoming bathhouse - Designboom
articles.title: Kengo Kuma's KAI Water Culture House Prepares to Open in Copenhagen
articles.excerpt: Designed by Kengo Kuma & Associates, the KAI Water Culture House on Copenhagen's Paper Island opens in December with five brick towers and ten pools.
articles.content: Kengo Kuma & Associates' KAI Water Culture House is scheduled to open on December 5, 2026, on Copenhagen's Papirøen. Spanning 5,800 square meters along the harborfront, the spa introduces ten swimming pools. The building is recognizable by five irregular brick towers rising above a glass base. Approximately 300,000 handmade bricks cover the angular surfaces in a stepped pattern that catches daylight. Across the facades, 403 windows bring light into the bathing areas and frame harbor views. The tallest volume, the Culture Tower, houses spaces for cultural activities and community gatherings. The Valley Pool, an open-air swimming basin, is positioned on the first floor between the five brick volumes under the sky. A heated outdoor onsen on the same level overlooks the harbor, drawing on Japanese bathing traditions. At ground level, the facility contains a 25-meter fitness pool, a teaching pool, and three smaller pools for children, while upper levels feature warmer bathing areas, a cold plunge pool, saunas, and a steam bath. The year-round pools are supported by a ground-source heat pump system connected to ten boreholes extending 250 meters below ground.

articles.originalTitle: HISTORICAL ARCHIVE | The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florenskij - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Venice Biennale Stages Pavel A. Florensky Project at Historical Archive
articles.excerpt: The Historical Archive of La Biennale di Venezia will present a five-day special project dedicated to Pavel A. Florensky, exploring the relationship between language and truth. The performances will take place from 16 to 20 November at the Arsenale.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia is presenting The Pillar and Ground of the Truth by Pavel A. Florensky as part of the Biennale of the Word. Taking place from 16 to 20 November 2026 at the new premises of the Historical Archive at the Arsenale, the project is conceived and directed by Antonello Pocetti across five evenings. The texts have been adapted from Florensky's writings to convey the depth of his reflections. Each evening opens with contributions from figures in culture, philosophy, and religion, followed by staged readings. Born in 1882 in Yevlakh, Azerbaijan, Florensky studied mathematics in Moscow before turning to philosophy and theology. Ordained an Orthodox priest in 1911, he engaged in research spanning mathematics, music, painting, and philosophy. Following the 1917 Revolution, he remained in Russia, where he participated in scientific projects before being arrested on counter-revolutionary charges and executed near Leningrad on 8 December 1937. Tickets become available starting 29 October on the La Biennale di Venezia website.

articles.originalTitle: Unboxing Victorian mourning: dress, human hair jewellery and postmortem photos - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Unboxes 19th Century Victorian Mourning Traditions
articles.excerpt: Victoria and Albert Museum curators released a video exploring 19th century mourning traditions, featuring human hair jewellery and postmortem photography.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum released a video examining 19th century mourning traditions. Curators Ruth and Lydia presented a genuine Victorian mourning outfit, intricate jewellery crafted from human hair, and postmortem photographs used to memorialise the deceased. The presentation highlights how grief, love, and art intertwined during the 19th century through jet jewellery, veils, and specific mourning cards. The video also explores the practice of Victorian postmortem photography, wherein families captured their final memories with departed loved ones. The institution utilizes third-party platforms to share content on its website, requiring user consent for targeting cookies. This digital release forms part of the museum's ongoing efforts to document and share its extensive collections and historical research with a wider public audience through online channels.

articles.originalTitle: Michele Bönan Has Been Designing Hotels for Over 50 Years. And Is Still at the Top of His Game - WWD
articles.title: Architect Michele Bönan Reflects on Five Decades of Hotel Design
articles.excerpt: Architect Michele Bönan, with a career spanning nearly 50 years, reflects on the evolution of luxury hospitality, noting that guests increasingly seek wellness, privacy, and a sense of belonging.
articles.content: Florence-based architect Michele Bönan, known for transforming historic spaces into cozy retreats, reflects on a career spanning nearly 50 years in hospitality design. Bönan observes that the definition of luxury has evolved, with guests increasingly prioritizing wellness, privacy, and a sense of belonging over impersonal grandeur. His signature aesthetic, blending Italian craftsmanship, contemporary art, antiques, and bespoke furnishings, has shaped properties for brands such as Rocco Forte Hotels and J.K. Place. Among recent projects, Bönan designed the Casa J.K. Place Roma residences within an 18th-century Roman palazzo, featuring custom details and materials. In 2021, he launched the Michele Bonan Interiors collection alongside his son, Sky Bönan. Currently, Bönan is working on restoring the historic Palazzo dei Principi Caravita di Sirignano in Naples, a regal residence with foundations laid in 1535, which is scheduled to open in 2027.

articles.originalTitle: Morphosis and Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates Reveal Design of Campus Expansion at the Perot Museum - Architectural Record
articles.title: Perot Museum Reveals Design for Campus Expansion Project in Dallas
articles.excerpt: The Perot Museum of Nature and Science in Dallas has revealed plans to transform four surrounding acres into an outdoor science destination. Designed by Morphosis and Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates, the project replaces surface parking with green space.
articles.content: The Perot Museum of Nature and Science in Dallas has unveiled plans to transform four acres surrounding its building into an outdoor science destination. Morphosis, designer of the original museum, leads the project alongside landscape architect Michael Van Valkenburgh Associates. Spanning approximately 60,000 square feet, the campus expansion will feature about 25 large-scale exhibits and 40 learning stations exploring natural forces such as wind, water, and weather. Planned attractions include a fire tornado, a giant water vortex, and a cloud maze. Shade trees, native plantings, and a pollinator habitat are integrated into the design. In addition to outdoor exhibits, the project includes a redesigned entrance and lobby, expanded educational, dining, and event spaces, and a new parking garage. The expansion forms part of the museum's $185 million Curiosity Unbound capital campaign, which has raised $135 million to date. Construction is expected to begin in early 2027 and reach completion in late 2028.

articles.originalTitle: Bernard Arnault on Craftsmanship, Creativity and Passion [PHOTOS] - WWD
articles.title: Photographs Highlighting Bernard Arnault, Craftsmanship, and Creativity Across LVMH
articles.excerpt: Newly released photographs trace Bernard Arnault s family background, workshop craftsmanship, and collaborations with architect Frank Gehry.
articles.content: A newly published visual collection sheds light on Bernard Arnault s personal history and professional engagements. The archival frames feature a childhood photograph of Arnault with his mother, Marie Josèphe Savinel, in 1950, alongside a 1953 portrait with his sister, Dominique, a 1958 family portrait, and an image with his grandfather at the family company around 1959. The collection also includes a 1967 photograph with his grandmother, Elisa Jeanne Gachon, and a 1969 portrait from his time at Ecole Polytechnique. Among the images are photographs of Arnault alongside architect Frank Gehry in front of the Fondation Louis Vuitton in Paris, as well as shots at the Institut de France de Paris. Additionally, the documented visuals encompass scenes from inside the Berluti atelier during the 2026 LVMH Journées Particulières, appearances by Antoine Arnault with the Chaumet team, and interior views of Tiffany and Bvlgari ateliers.

articles.originalTitle: Unique collection of historic Anglo-Indian artworks gifted to Tate by Charles Greig – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Charles Greig Gifts 18th and 19th-Century Anglo-Indian Artworks to Tate
articles.excerpt: Art historian Charles Greig has donated a collection of 50 artworks dating from the 18th and 19th centuries to Tate. The works will be displayed at Tate Britain in 2028.
articles.content: Tate has received a collection of 50 artworks from the 18th and 19th centuries, donated outright by art historian and scholar Charles Greig. Gifted without tax incentives, the collection comprises oil paintings, watercolours, and miniatures that reflect the cultural and political changes during British colonialism in South Asia. Assembled over four decades, the collection features works by Indian artists such as Sita Ram and Ghulam Ali Khan, alongside European creators including Johan Zoffany, Rudolph Swoboda, William Hodges, and the Daniell brothers. Key highlights include Johan Zoffany's 1784 portrait of Prince Jawan Bakht and Rudolph Swoboda's Sepoy painting, introducing Company paintings to Tate's holdings for the first time. Tate Britain Director Alex Farquharson noted that the acquisition strengthens the museum's representation of art from the British Empire. Charles Greig expressed satisfaction in ensuring the collection remains preserved and accessible to the public. The works will be exhibited for the first time in a dedicated free display at Tate Britain in 2028.

articles.originalTitle: TATE ACQUIRES NEW WORKS FOR THE UNIQUE COLLECTION OF HISTORIC ANGLO-INDIAN ARTWORKS GIFTED TO TATE BY CHARLES GREIG – Press Release - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Acquires an Exceptional Collection of 50 Historic Anglo-Indian Artworks
articles.excerpt: Art historian Charles Greig has gifted 50 18th and 19th-century Anglo-Indian artworks to Tate, with a dedicated public display planned for 2028.
articles.content: Tate has received a collection of 50 artworks by artists who lived and worked in India during the 18th and 19th centuries, gifted outright by art historian Charles Greig. Made without tax incentives, the philanthropic donation reflects the cultural, social, and political changes brought by British colonialism in South Asia. Greig's collection comprises oil paintings, watercolours, and miniatures built over four decades. It features works by Indian artists such as Sita Ram and Ghulam Ali Khan alongside European and British artists like Johan Zoffany, Rudolf Swoboda, William Hodges, Thomas Daniell, and William Daniell. Key highlights include Zoffany's 1784 portrait of Prince Jawan Bakht, Swoboda's c.1886 Sepoy portrait, and three watercolours by Sita Ram. Tate Britain Director Alex Farquharson noted that the gift will strengthen holdings of art produced in the British Empire. The public will first see the works in 2028 at a dedicated free display at Tate Britain.

articles.originalTitle: Brand new museums deserve brand new approaches to wayfinding with Fieldwork Facility - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Sustainable Wayfinding and Signage Approach for V&A East Sites
articles.excerpt: Design studio Fieldwork Facility developed a modular, lower-impact wayfinding and signage system across V&A East Storehouse, the David Bowie Centre, and V&A East Museum to reduce environmental impact.
articles.content: Working across the V&A East Storehouse, David Bowie Centre, and V&A East Museum, Hackney-based design studio Fieldwork Facility combined creative design with sustainability strategies to reduce the environmental impact of wayfinding, labelling, and interpretation. The studio utilized lower-impact materials designed to minimise waste and maximise reuse through a modular system where signs can be disassembled, updated, and recycled. At V&A East Storehouse, primary signage utilizes recycled composite paper blocks, recycled plastics for lettering, aluminium cases, and enameled lava-stone roundels. V&A East Museum features a distinct style combining European sycamore wood instead of imported bamboo to lower shipping emissions, alongside recycled plastics. To address the widespread museum challenge of single-use plastic vinyl graphics, Fieldwork Facility painted graphics directly onto walls and created 1,240 hand-finished tiles from wood and recycled plastics for temporary exhibitions. Narrow scrolling LED ticker displays were additionally introduced for real-time event information. Despite extensive efforts to eliminate single-use vinyl, approximately 6 square meters of vinyl was retained exclusively for booking QR codes.

articles.originalTitle: Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography Exhibition Guide - tate.org.uk
articles.title: Tate Modern Exhibition Explores the Origins of Art Photography
articles.excerpt: Tate Modern is hosting Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography, an exhibition exploring pictorialism. The showcase features over 200 rare vintage prints and runs through February 2027.
articles.content: Tate Modern is hosting a major exhibition titled Light and Magic: The Birth of Art Photography, which examines pictorialism, the first international art photography movement. Running from 14 October 2026 to 21 February 2027, the exhibition brings together over 200 rare vintage photographic prints from around the world. Beginning in the 1880s, pictorialist photographers sought to establish photography as a genuine art form comparable to painting, employing imaginative darkroom techniques and expressive compositions. The showcase highlights diverse analogue processes, including platinum prints, bromoil prints, and photogravures, alongside a functioning darkroom where visitors can learn environmentally friendly developing techniques on select days. Featured creators include Alvin Langdon Coburn, Soichi Sunami, and members of the Brazilian group Foto Cine Clube Bandeirante, who expanded the movement's modernist possibilities across decades. Tickets are available for purchase, and admission is free for museum members, who can also access a smartphone audio guide.

articles.originalTitle: EXCLUSIVE: DeMellier Opens Its First Store in London’s Sloane Square, Designed to Feel Like a Stylish Home - WWD
articles.title: Luxury Handbag Brand DeMellier Opens First Store in London's Sloane Square
articles.excerpt: Approaching its 10th anniversary, luxury handbag brand DeMellier has opened its first stand-alone store in London's Sloane Square, designed to evoke a warm, residential atmosphere.
articles.content: Approaching its 10th anniversary, luxury handbag brand DeMellier has opened its inaugural stand-alone store in London's Sloane Square. Founder Mireia Llusia-Lindh collaborated with residential architect Nicolas Schuybroek to fashion a 3,230-square-foot space across two floors that mimics a stylish home rather than a traditional retail environment. The ground floor resembles a living room where handbags are displayed on marble shelves, while the lower level features a dining table format and a craft corner displaying leather-cutting tools, needles, and artisan films. The interior incorporates oak floors, mineral plaster walls, and abstract paintings by British artist Susan Gunn. Operating primarily as an online business that accounts for 80 percent of its sales, the profitable company closed its financial year with 56 million pounds in revenue. DeMellier employs responsibly sourced leather and contributes a portion of every sale to SOS Children’s Villages through its philanthropic initiative to support children in need.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Beverly Buchanan - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 to Feature Works by Beverly Buchanan
articles.excerpt: The Central Pavilion at the Venice Biennale hosts an exhibition of drawings, paintings, sculptures, and earthworks by artist Beverly Buchanan, exploring Southern building traditions, land ownership, and custodianship histories.
articles.content: The 2026 edition of the Venice Biennale presents the artistic practice of Beverly Buchanan, who was born in Fuquay, USA, in 1940 and died in Ann Arbor in 2015. Hosted at the Central Pavilion, the presentation encompasses drawings, paintings, sculptures, and earthworks by the artist. Buchanan's practice engages with histories of custodianship, land ownership, and architectural vernaculars, specifically through the prism of Black Southern building traditions. After earning master's degrees in parasitology and public health at Columbia University and exhibiting in New York City, Buchanan returned to the American South in 1977, living in Georgia before relocating to Michigan in 2010. The exhibition emphasizes the artist's voice as constructed through her writing, research notes, and fieldwork. Her short accompanying texts combine biography and invention to gather testimonies from individuals within and around her community. Utilizing diverse materials ranging from thrifted timbers and metals to medical spatulas, bottle caps, and concrete admixtures, Buchanan acknowledged the historical and social relativity of each medium. Her shack sculptures enact cultural preservation as a method, commemorating figures such as self-taught architect Mary Lou Furcron and artist Nellie Mae Rowe. Furthermore, her concrete and tabby works—incorporating oyster shells, water, sand, and ash—invoke the material economy and historical consciousness of coastal Georgia's survival.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | Issa Samb - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Biennale Arte 2026 Features Installations Dedicated to Issa Samb
articles.excerpt: The 2026 edition of Biennale Arte presents installations inspired by the Dakar courtyard of Senegallist artist Issa Samb, highlighting his multidisciplinary practice and grassroots artistic philosophy.
articles.content: Born in Dakar in 1945 and passing away there in 2017, Senegallist artist Issa Samb is featured in the Central Pavilion and Arsenale during Biennale Arte 2026. Hailing from the Lebou community of sanctuary keepers, Samb worked across painting, collage, assemblage, sculpture, performance, and writing. He co-founded the Laboratoire Agit'Art collective with filmmaker Djibril Diop Mambéty and others, championing a grassroots, autonomous approach focused on public engagement rather than conventional cultural politics. His presence at the 2026 Biennale is articulated through installations inspired by his central Dakar home and courtyard, La Cour, which historically served as a meeting place for artistic and political thought. The presentation features costumes, suspended objects, assemblages, notes, and sketches. Additionally, a video contribution by Adrienne Edwards documents a visit to La Cour, while Ican Ramageli's film Cap Vers l’Est portrays Samb exploring liminal spaces where the living meets the dead. The exhibition runs from May through November.

articles.originalTitle: Obama Presidential Center Reaches $1B in Total Costs - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Obama Presidential Center Reaches $1 Billion in Total Costs
articles.excerpt: The total cost of the Barack Obama Presidential Center in Chicago has reached approximately $1 billion, compared to its original $350 million budget.
articles.content: The campus cost of the Barack Obama Presidential Center on Chicago's South Side has reached $1 billion. According to the latest filing from the non-profit Obama Foundation, this latest figure is about $91 million above the September projection of $909 million, excluding $123 million in publicly financed infrastructure improvements. Emily Bittner, the foundation's vice president of communications, stated that the costs are raised through private contributions. The foundation stated it has no outstanding disputed charges with Lakeside Alliance, the joint venture contractor that completed the main building. The project's budget was originally announced as $350 million, jumped to $500 million when design was completed in 2017, and reached $850 million in early September before the latest filing. The recent increases were attributed to additional construction scope such as the Home Court basketball center, public art, and insurance.
